# Exact cap integrals after the thin-edge missed-fiber phase

This note gives exact formulas for testing continuation of the d=4 thin-edge family. It does NOT classify its entire active family after the already certified small-delta regime, and it does not claim a new counterexample or a universal 1/e floor. The formulas isolate the actual changes that any such classification must retain.

Use the simplex T and symmetric endpoint body D_delta of `candidate e52160c774656005`, with J={0,1}, H=lambda_0+lambda_1, and D_delta={H>=1-delta}. Write l=1-delta, alpha=4delta^3-3delta^4, and a candidate symmetric mark as

    y=(x,x,z,z,z),  2x+3z=1.

All integrals below are ordinary h=0 volumes, divided by V=|T|. They describe a possible limiting branch; positive-width attainment and convergence require the separate actual active-family proof.

## 1. Low-vertex caps with actual endpoint intersections

For i in {2,3,4}, consider a cap at zero integer tilt with equation

    lambda_i+cH >= z+2cx.

Put

    u=1-c>0,  r=1-z-2cx=2z+2xu,
    t=r/u=2x+2z/u.

Assume 0<r<min(1,u), so the cap strictly isolates vertex i in T. Its four edge intercepts are t,t,r,r; therefore its own volume is

    q_L = r^4/u^2 = u^2 t^4.                          (1)

Map a reference simplex onto this cap. The sum of its two high-coordinate barycentrics has the Beta(2,3) law, and physical H equals t times that sum. Its survival function at s in[0,1] is

    B(s)=(1-s)^3(1+3s)=1-6s^2+8s^3-3s^4.

Thus the exact endpoint intersection is

    q_D=0                       if t<=l,
    q_D=u^2(t-l)^3(t+3l)        if t>l.                (2)

The zero-base-tilt cap mass in all three fibers is

    Q_L=u^2 A(t),
    A(t)=t^4                           if t<=l,
         3t^4-12l^2t^2+16l^3t-6l^4    if t>l.         (3)

This accounts for BOTH endpoint contributions. Discarding them past t=l would be the old phase error.

As a function of its threshold with c fixed, the endpoint mass in this vertex chamber is

    [(r-ul)_+]^3(r+3ul)/u^2.

For r>ul its second derivative in r is12(r^2-u^2l^2)/u^2>=0, and it joins zero with two zero derivatives. Consequently the endpoint tail is convex in threshold within this chamber. This proves local optimality of zero integer tilt there by Jensen, but does NOT establish global optimality among tilts that leave the chamber.

## 2. The exact continuous stationarity equation in this branch

For fixed x,z, u=2z/(t-2x). Hence

    Q_L(t)=4z^2 A(t)/(t-2x)^2.

An interior stationary low-vertex cap satisfies

    A'(t)(t-2x)-2A(t)=0.                              (4)

Before endpoint contact, (4) gives t=4x, the old centroid-section cap. After endpoint contact t>l, it becomes the quartic equation

    3t^4-12xt^3+(24xl^2-8l^3)t-16xl^3+6l^4=0,

or equivalently

    x=[3t^4-8l^3t+6l^4]/[4(3t^3-6l^2t+4l^3)].       (5)

These are exact polynomial identities. Their geometric meaning is that the kernel section centroid uses the middle section AND both endpoint sections. It is no longer the own-section-centroid equation from the old branch.

## 3. A second necessary phase check: high-vertex saturation

If a high-vertex cap remains at its own centroid-section direction and its integer tilt saturates exactly one endpoint, its own mass is

    q_H=256xz^3,

and its total mass is q_H+alpha. At zero integer tilt its D_delta intersection is

    q_H F(delta/(4z)),
    F(s)=4s^3-3s^4 for0<=s<=1,  F(s)=1 for s>=1.       (6)

This follows from the Beta(3,2) law of the low-coordinate sum in that high-vertex cap, whose three low edge intercepts are4z. Therefore saturation can be active only if

    alpha <= 2q_H F(delta/(4z)).                      (7)

If (7) fails, zero base tilt is an explicit strictly cheaper competitor. Even when (7) holds, other nonsaturating tilts still need to be checked. Thus the old high-cap saturation formula cannot be continued arbitrarily toward delta=1.

A candidate five-cap branch with two saturated high caps and three zero-base-tilt low caps must satisfy both (4) and the common-mass equation

    Q_L=q_H+alpha.                                   (8)

Equations (4),(7),(8) are necessary checks, not an assertion that the corresponding caps are all actual global minima.

## 4. Exact response weights, conditional on this being the actual branch

Suppose the branch just described is actual, all caps are strict vertex cuts, and its symmetry-averaged balanced menu consists of the two high caps and three low caps. Let w_H be each high response weight and w_L each low weight, so2w_H+3w_L=1.

The high-cap response vector is its affine normal times4q_H. The total low coarea in the chosen scale is

    S_L=u A'(t)=Q_L/z,

where the second equality follows from (4). Its affine normal has coefficient c on the two high coordinates, coefficient one at its retained low vertex, and zero at the other low vertices. Balancing the high and low coordinate sums gives

    w_H/w_L = S_L(1-3c)/[q_H(2/z-1/x)],
    c=1-u.                                         (9)

The right side must be positive for a positive five-cap menu. The factor S_L includes both endpoint coareas; replacing it by the middle coarea would give incorrect weights.

## 5. Two explicit fields that any 1/e obstruction on this branch must defeat

First choose a constant physical field at the normal of the high facet F_0. Its middle capture integral, divided by |F_0|, is

    w_H(4z)^3+3w_L u^2t^3.

The two endpoint shared patches have total area2delta^3|F_0|. Their high-cap capture sum is2w_H delta^3|F_0|. Each low cap's intersection with one such patch has relative area u^2(t-l)^3, because its one surviving high coordinate has a Beta(1,3) tail. Therefore the exact efficiency is

    R_H = [w_H(4z)^3+3w_Lu^2t^3
           +2w_Hdelta^3+6w_Lu^2(t-l)^3]
          /[1+2delta^3].                            (10)

Second, symmetry of the two endpoint fibers allows BOTH saturated high caps to be chosen to capture the LEFT endpoint. This changes neither their continuous response vectors nor their masses. Choose a normal-dependent field supported at D_delta's truncating-facet normal, and multiply it by the globally convex nonnegative base function[-z_base]_+. It isolates that exposed left endpoint.

On its truncating facet H=l, the low coordinates are uniform on a2-simplex of total delta, independently of the high split. Each low cap occupies the fraction

    [u(t-l)/delta]^2

of that facet. Its efficiency is consequently

    R_E=2w_H+3w_L[u(t-l)/delta]^2.                    (11)

In particular it is at least2w_H. Formula (11) gives a legitimate BEST-menu lower bound: the two high caps may be retargeted to the same endpoint because the assumed branch uses exact saturated minima, while the three low caps keep zero base tilt.

Thus a genuine individual-capacity counterexample below1/e on this particular post-contact branch would require BOTH R_H<1/e and R_E<1/e, in addition to a complete active-normal and integer-tilt classification. No such simultaneous certified inequality is proved here. The purpose of these equations is to prevent a false continuation that counts the extra endpoint volume in the denominator while forgetting its coarea, response-weight, and selective-facet benefits.
